extracted.intended_audience: government policymakers designing consultations and stakeholders (citizens, businesses, NGOs, employees, consumers, public sector, international partners) preparing submissions to regulatory consultations
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and checklist for stakeholders and agencies on producing and evaluating high-quality inputs to regulatory consultations, emphasizing early engagement, specificity, appropriate channels, and evidence. Applicable to public comments and broader stakeholder engagement across regulatory processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early Consultation on Problem Definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Consultations conducted at the policy-problem-definition stage produce better evidence than consultations on draft proposals alone. A high-quality stakeholder input contributes at this stage, not just on the formal draft.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage before a draft proposal exists so your input can shape problem framing and options. The OECD emphasises that consulting at problem-definition yields better evidence; therefore submissions that identify problems and propose early-stage input are higher value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversified Channels of Input
rubrics_metrics.description: Consultations should use multiple formats — surveys, focus groups, written submissions, roundtables — to capture different stakeholder voices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the mix of channels offered by the consultation to reach different audiences and to submit input in the format best suited to the evidence and perspective you bring. Agencies should design consultations with varied channels; stakeholders should choose the appropriate channel(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent Mechanisms Showing How Feedback Shaped the Final Result
rubrics_metrics.description: Stakeholders should be able to see how their input affected the outcome. Effective submissions therefore should be specific enough that the agency can cite them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make submissions concrete and attributable (e.g., include numbered recommendations, specific references to the consultation text) so that they can be traced and quoted in outcome reports. This aids transparency and demonstrates impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feedback to Participants
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide post-consultation feedback to participants; the OECD identifies this as the area of greatest deficit globally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should publish outcome/response documents explaining how submissions were considered and why decisions were made. For stakeholders, requesting or seeking such feedback helps close the loop and improves future engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage at the Earliest Practical Stage
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the input engage at the earliest practical stage of regulatory development?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer contributions made at problem-definition or policy-design stages rather than only responding to near-final drafts. Early-stage engagement increases the likelihood submissions influence policy framing and options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specificity for Citable Input
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the input specific enough to be cited in the consultation outcome report?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear, concrete proposals, citeable language, and explicit links to the consultation questions or text. Avoid vague statements; include proposed wording, metrics, or rules where relevant so agencies can reference your submission directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify Stakeholder Category and Interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the input clearly identify the stakeholder category and interests represented?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State who you represent (citizen, business, consumer, employee org, NGO, public sector, international partner, etc.), any relevant conflicts of interest, and the perspective or constituency behind the views. This helps agencies assess representativeness and weight of evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge Consultation Objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the input acknowledge the consultation's stated objectives?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show that you have read and understood the consultation's goals; align or explain divergence between your input and stated objectives. Explicitly addressing the consultation questions increases usefulness to policymakers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Offered Channels Appropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the input use one of the consultation's offered channels appropriately?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow channel-specific instructions (e.g., survey format, response fields, deadlines, attendance rules for roundtables). Using an inappropriate channel or ignoring submission format reduces the likelihood your input is processed and considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide Proportionate Evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the input provide evidence (data, examples, expert opinion) proportionate to the claim?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support assertions with relevant data, case studies, or authoritative expertise; the level of evidence should match the importance and specificity of the claim. Where empirical evidence is limited, clearly label opinion vs. evidence and explain the basis for conclusions.
